newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA'S CONGRESS GALVANISED BY SONIA GANDHI.
newsitem.headline: INDIA'S CONGRESS GALVANISED BY SONIA GANDHI.

text.p: India's oldest party, Congress, is looking to the popular widow of Rajiv Gandhi and the inheritor of the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty to lead it back to power after an embarrassing electoral drubbing last year.
But party leaders say they are in no hurry and will need a year to 18 months to gird themselves for a stab at power.

Sonia Gandhi stole the limelight at the party's three-day plenary meeting ending on Sunday in Calcutta. Thousands clapped wildly and shouted when she appeared on Saturday and made a speech that brought delegates to their feet.
"Soniaji, do whatever you feel, but don't break the link with Congress," party president Sitaram Kesri said. "You are a source of strength and inspiration to Congress."

Congress activists said the party would eventually emerge as an alternative to Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's increasingly fractious coalition government, which ranges from free market advocates to communists.

Congress finished a humble second in last year's polls but remains the power behind Gujral's government as it provides the votes in parliament needed to survive against the Hindu nationalist opposition.
Sonia Gandhi's appearance energised the rank and file who want her to quit her drawing room in New Delhi and take up the 112-year-old party's banner.

"She represents a family which has provided inspiration to the party for four generations and what you saw was a manifestation of that," Congress leader Madhavrao Scindia told Reuters after the 50-year-old widow addressed the meeting.

Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated by a suicide bomber in the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu while campaigning for general elections in 1991. His mother, Indira Gandhi, and her father, Jawaharlal Nehru, both served as prime minister.
Since her husband's death, Sonia Gandhi has wielded power from behind closed doors at her residence at 10 Janpath in the capital, but she came out of the political closet in May to join Congress.
"After the death of Rajiv Gandhi there was no leader. Sonia can lead Congress in a new direction," said Mohammed Akram, a Congress worker from the central state of Madhya Pradesh.
Kesri, who was elected party president in June, sensed the change in the mood of party workers and urged Sonia Gandhi to guide the organisation out of its current crisis.
"Soniaji will definitely strengthen the party," said Congress leader Motilal Vohra.

Once the standard-bearer for the independence movement and the political home of Mahatma Gandhi, Congress was battered in last year's general elections after a number of leaders were named in corruption cases.
Now the party is in a hurry to clean its tarnished image but in no rush to face the electorate as it recuperates.
"I think we need a little more time and provided we concentrate on the organisation, I don't see any reason why we should not win the next election," Scindia said.
"When elections come after one or 1-1/2 years, your leader will hoist the national flag on the Red Fort," Kesri said on Friday.
Every year the prime minister unfurls the flag from the ramparts of Delhi's Red Fort on August 15, Independence Day.
